title: Alice Goodman
gist: This is an author archive/index page for Prospect columnist Alice Goodman, a poet, librettist and Anglican priest, not a standalone article — it lists her bio and 'Clerical life' column headlines on identity, institutional strain and faith in the Church of England, with no article body to analyze.

insights.claim: Alice Goodman is a poet, librettist and Anglican priest based in Cambridgeshire who writes Prospect's 'Clerical life' column, giving a rare institutional-insider perspective on the Church of England.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Positions her commentary on the Church as coming from a practicing clergy member rather than an outside commentator, which matters when weighing the credibility of any institutional claims she makes.
insights.quote: Alice Goodman is a poet, librettist and Anglican priest in Cambridgeshire

insights.claim: One of Goodman's listed column headlines states directly that 'The Church of England is running out of wardens,' pointing to a volunteer/staffing shortage within the institution.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Flags a specific institutional resourcing problem inside the Church of England worth following up on directly, though only the headline is available here, not the article text.

insights.claim: Goodman's column headlines recur around themes of identity strain within the clergy — from having to 'abandon' a former identity to become a priest, to arguing 'Jesus isn't manly enough for the far right,' to using 'hope' as an explicit antidote to climate despair — suggesting a consistent editorial thread about the Church's struggle to stay culturally relevant.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Suggests a recurring narrative at Prospect about institutional religion's identity crisis relative to secular and far-right cultural currents, useful context for any single Goodman column.
